issues.title: Hardcoded devtools loading message text
issues.description: The rule requires all user-facing strings to be defined in web/i18n/en-US/ translation files and accessed via useTranslation hook. The code hardcodes 'Loading devtools...' directly in the JSX instead of using a translation key.
issues.rule_name: Frontend User-Facing Strings Must Use i18n Translations

issues.title: Devtools rendered before application children causes layout issues
issues.description: The TanStackDevtoolsLoader is now rendered before the children components in the QueryClientProvider. This reverses the intended rendering order from the original PR, which had devtools after children. When devtools mount first, they may inject DOM elements before the main application content is rendered, potentially causing layout shifts, visual flashes, or z-index conflicts. Devtools should be rendered as a sibling after main content to avoid interfering with the initial application layout and rendering.

issues.title: Missing error logging in TanStack devtools lazy import
issues.description: The TanStackDevtoolsLoader silently swallows import errors without logging them, making it impossible to debug why the devtools fail to load. This creates an inconsistent error handling pattern compared to the ReactScanLoader (in the same PR), which properly logs errors with console.error before returning a fallback component. When developers encounter issues with TanStack devtools not appearing, they will have no visibility into whether it's due to an import failure, missing dependencies, or other issues.

issues.title: console.error violates Frontend Code Must Not Use console Statements rule
issues.description: The ReactScanLoader uses console.error which directly violates Rule 25 from AGENTS.md added in this same PR. The rule explicitly states that production frontend code must avoid console.log, console.warn, and console.error statements as enforced by the no-console warning rule. This creates an inconsistency where the code violates a compliance rule that was just introduced, and creates inconsistent error handling compared to TanStackDevtoolsLoader which silently catches errors. The use of console statements in production code should be replaced with proper logging mechanisms.

issues.title: console.error used in frontend code
issues.description: Rule 25 prohibits console statements in frontend code. The added code logs an error with console.error when lazy-loading fails.
issues.rule_name: Frontend Code Must Not Use console Statements

pr.title: Code Review Bench PR #30318 - refactor(web): organize devtools components
pr.author: unknown

structured_output.summary:
This PR moves the React Scan and TanStack devtools into per-tool folders under `web/app/components/devtools/`, and adds a `Loader` component for each. Each loader gates on `IS_DEV`, lazy-loads the real implementation, and wraps it in `Suspense`. `layout.tsx` and `context/query-client.tsx` now render the loaders instead of importing the devtools directly. The two files are pure renames (100% similarity), and the only real logic is in the two new loaders.

The core design holds up. Both loaders return `null` before rendering the lazy component, so the `import()` never runs in production, and the `react-scan` package is no longer imported eagerly by the root layout. I grepped the head commit and found no stale references to the old `components/devtools.tsx` or `components/react-scan.tsx` paths. The remaining issues are small: the two loaders handle import failures differently, and the dev-only fallback renders visible text. The PR description also mentions a `devtools/index.ts` barrel that is not in the diff.
structured_output.verdictRationale: No critical or high-severity problems. The production gating is correct, the lazy imports are only triggered in development, and the renames are complete. What remains is a low-severity inconsistency in error handling between the two loaders and a small dev-only UI flash, both easy to follow up on.

architecture.overview:
Before this PR, `web/app/layout.tsx` statically imported `ReactScan` from `components/react-scan.tsx`, and `web/context/query-client.tsx` lazily imported `TanStackDevtoolsWrapper` from `components/devtools.tsx` behind an inline `IS_DEV &&` check. The React Scan library was therefore bundled into the root layout's import graph even though it only runs in development. The TanStack devtools were already lazy, but the gating and the `Suspense` wiring lived in the context file.

The PR moves each tool into its own folder (`devtools/react-scan/`, `devtools/tanstack/`) and adds a `Loader` per tool. The loader owns the `IS_DEV` check, the `lazy()` import with a `.catch` fallback, and the `Suspense` boundary. The layout and the query-client provider now render only the loader. Because the loader returns `null` before rendering the lazy component, the dynamic import is not executed in production, and the devtools code is split into separate chunks.
steps: Entry points are unchanged in shape: `web/app/layout.tsx` renders `<ReactScanLoader />` once in the body, and `web/context/query-client.tsx` renders `<TanStackDevtoolsLoader />` inside `QueryClientProvider`.
`react-scan/loader.tsx` (new) returns `null` unless `IS_DEV`. Otherwise it renders a `Suspense` boundary around a `lazy()` import of `./scan`, with a visible 'Loading devtools...' fallback.
`react-scan/scan.tsx` is the old `components/react-scan.tsx`, moved unchanged. It calls `scan()` from `react-scan` in a `useEffect` and renders `null`.
`tanstack/loader.tsx` (new) follows the same pattern. It lazy-imports `./devtools` with a silent `.catch` and uses a `null` fallback.
`tanstack/devtools.tsx` is the old `components/devtools.tsx`, moved unchanged. It renders `TanStackDevtools` with the React Query and Form plugins.

findings.title: Loaders handle import failures inconsistently
findings.fixPrompt: In `web/app/components/devtools/tanstack/loader.tsx`, the `.catch` on the lazy import (around lines 9-11) silently returns an empty component. Change it to accept the error and call `console.error` with a message like 'Failed to load TanStack devtools:', then return the same empty fallback. Match the pattern used by the `.catch` in `web/app/components/devtools/react-scan/loader.tsx` (lines 9-11) so both loaders behave the same way.

findings.title: Dev-only 'Loading devtools...' text flashes in the page body
findings.fixPrompt: In `web/app/components/devtools/react-scan/loader.tsx`, the `Suspense` fallback on line 20 renders a visible 'Loading devtools...' div. Since `ReactScan` in `scan.tsx` renders `null` and this is a dev-only tool, change the fallback to `null` to match `tanstack/loader.tsx`. This avoids a stray text node in the layout during dev chunk loading.

findings.title: Production gating prevents devtools chunks from loading
findings.body:
Both loaders return `null` when `IS_DEV` is false, before the `Suspense` tree that renders the `lazy()` component is reached. React only runs a lazy factory on first render, so `import('./scan')` and `import('./devtools')` never execute in production. The `react-scan` package is also no longer imported eagerly by `web/app/layout.tsx`, which was the main bundle-size concern in the old code.

::diff{file="web/app/components/devtools/react-scan/loader.tsx" lines="15-17"}

findings.title: Renamed files are complete with no stale imports
findings.body:
The two moved files are exact renames (100% similarity), so the logic is unchanged. I searched the head commit for the old paths (`components/react-scan`, `components/devtools`) and found no remaining references. `query-client.tsx` and `layout.tsx` now import the loaders by their new paths. Because `components/devtools.tsx` is gone, the old `@/app/components/devtools` import would have failed to resolve, but nothing still imports it.
